interactions.label: Which histological finding is characteristic of pilomatricoma?

params.question: Which histological finding is characteristic of pilomatricoma?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tadpole-shaped ducts are the hallmark of syringoma, an eccrine adnexal tumour arising from sweat gland differentiation.

answers.text: Jigsaw-shaped basaloid islands with a pink hyaline sheath

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This pattern describes cylindroma (turban tumour), an adnexal tumour of apocrine lineage — not pilomatricoma.
Correct. Pilomatricoma shows shadow (ghost) cells — eosinophilic cells whose nuclei have been replaced by a central pallor — alongside calcification, reflecting hair matrix differentiation.
Horn cysts scattered among bland basaloid keratinocytes are the hallmark of seborrheic keratosis, a benign epidermal tumour with a stuck-on appearance.

overallFeedback.feedback: The adnexal tumour triad links one histological pattern to each tumour: tadpole-shaped ducts identify syringoma, jigsaw basaloid islands with a pink hyaline sheath identify cylindroma, and ghost cells with calcification identify pilomatricoma.
Correct! Remember the adnexal triad: tadpole ducts = syringoma, jigsaw islands with hyaline sheath = cylindroma, ghost cells with calcification = pilomatricoma.

params.question: A 65-year-old renal transplant recipient develops a firm, ulcerated plaque on their sun-exposed forearm. Which combination of risk factors most completely explains their susceptibility to squamous cell carcinoma?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PTCH1 mutation drives basal cell carcinoma through the Hedgehog signalling pathway. Intermittent UV is the trigger for BCC and melanoma — SCC follows chronic cumulative UV exposure instead.

answers.text: Chronic UV exposure and impaired immune surveillance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Chronic cumulative UV causes TP53 mutations in keratinocytes, while post-transplant immunosuppression (raising risk 65-fold) impairs clearance of these damaged cells, allowing stepwise progression to invasive SCC.
BRAF V600E is the driver mutation in approximately half of cutaneous melanomas, triggered by intermittent intense UV — neither mechanism is central to SCC pathogenesis.

answers.text: CDKN2A loss and neural crest cell migration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CDKN2A (p16) loss drives melanoma progression in the dysplastic naevus pathway, and neural crest origin is a melanocyte property — neither is relevant to SCC arising from keratinocytes.

overallFeedback.feedback: SCC develops through chronic cumulative UV causing TP53 mutations in keratinocytes. Post-transplant immunosuppression raises risk 65-fold by impairing immune clearance of UV-damaged cells. The other options describe BCC (PTCH1) or melanoma (BRAF, CDKN2A) pathways.

Correct! SCC requires chronic cumulative UV driving TP53 mutations, and immunosuppression removes the surveillance that would normally eliminate damaged keratinocytes — hence the 65-fold risk increase in transplant recipients.

params.question: In a benign melanocytic naevus, which histological feature confirms normal maturation?

answers.text: Melanocyte nests confined exclusively to the dermo-epidermal junction

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the location of a junctional naevus but says nothing about maturation. Maturation concerns cell size and pigmentation changes with depth, not nest location.

answers.text: Cells become progressively smaller and less pigmented with increasing depth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Maturation is the central concept in naevus assessment — in benign naevi, naevus cells become smaller, less pigmented, and more dispersed as they extend deeper into the dermis. Failure of this pattern is an alarm signal for melanoma.

answers.text: Uniform melanocyte size throughout all layers of the dermis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Uniform cell size throughout the dermis actually represents failure of maturation. In a benign naevus, cells should become progressively smaller with depth — uniformity at depth raises concern for malignancy.

answers.text: Increased melanin production in the deepest cell nests

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The opposite is expected. Normal maturation means deeper cells produce less melanin and become smaller. Retained or increased pigmentation at depth suggests loss of maturation and potential malignant transformation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Normal maturation means naevus cells become smaller and less pigmented as they extend deeper into the dermis. Loss of this maturation pattern — large, pigmented cells persisting at depth — is an important alarm signal for melanoma.

Correct! Maturation — the progressive decrease in cell size and pigmentation with depth — is the hallmark of benign behaviour. When deep cells remain large and pigmented, suspect malignant transformation.

params.question: A patient has two lesions biopsied simultaneously: an ulcerated plaque showing keratin pearls with intercellular bridges, and a pearly nodule showing peripheral palisading with retraction clefts. Based on metastatic behaviour, which lesion warrants more aggressive staging?

answers.text: The ulcerated plaque, as SCC carries a 5–10% metastatic risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Keratin pearls and intercellular bridges identify SCC, which metastasises in 5–10% of cases via lymphatics and blood. BCC (peripheral palisading, retraction cleft) is locally destructive but almost never metastasises — staging is therefore more critical for SCC.

answers.text: The pearly nodule, as BCC frequently metastasises to regional lymph nodes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BCC almost never metastasises despite being the most common skin malignancy. It earns the name 'rodent ulcer' for local destruction, not distant spread. SCC is the keratinocyte cancer requiring metastatic staging.

answers.text: Both require identical staging, as their metastatic rates are comparable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Their metastatic behaviour differs fundamentally. SCC carries a genuine 5–10% metastatic risk requiring staging workup, while BCC's near-zero metastatic rate means local control is usually sufficient.

answers.text: Neither requires staging, as skin cancers are managed by local excision alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While local excision may suffice for BCC, SCC's 5–10% metastatic rate necessitates staging — particularly with high-risk features such as poor differentiation, perineural invasion, or immunosuppression.

overallFeedback.feedback: SCC (keratin pearls, intercellular bridges) carries a 5–10% metastatic rate and requires staging workup. BCC (peripheral palisading, retraction clefts) almost never metastasises — it destroys locally but does not spread. This fundamental difference directly guides management.

Correct! SCC's 5–10% metastatic rate makes staging essential, while BCC's near-zero metastatic risk usually allows management by local control alone. This is one of the sharpest clinical distinctions between the two keratinocyte cancers.
